https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c998.text: Image source, Zelenskiy / Official Image caption, President Zelensky described the latest Ukrainian strikes as "our long-range sanctions" against Russian facilities he says finance Moscow's war By Jaroslav Lukiv Published 3 hours ago Ukraine has said it carried out overnight strikes deep inside Russia, hitting a major oil refinery and an airfield that houses Russian strategic aviation. President Volodymyr Zelensky said the Engels airfield and the refinery, both in the Saratov region some 600km (373miles) from Ukraine's border, were hit. An oil depot was also struck in Kaluga region and a drone launch site in Bryansk. Russia said eight people were killed in the Ukrainian strikes, and 635 drones shot down or intercepted. It also reported yet another strike on a warehouse of Russia's biggest online retailer Wildberries. Meanwhile, Moscow said its forces attacked overnight two Ukrainian ports and two vessels in the Black Sea. Later on Sunday, Ukraine said one person was killed in a Russian strike on a postal terminal near the north-eastern city of Kharkiv. Both Russia and Ukraine have recently intensified attacks focusing on major cities, energy facilities and warehouses, as the vast front line remains virtually static and US-led mediation attempts to end the war have shown no breakthrough. Russian President Vladimir Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Trump now 'not sure' about letting Ukraine build Patriot missiles Published 1 day ago Nine killed in strikes on Kyiv, as Ukraine sinks Russian container ship Published 1 day ago In Sunday's post on social media, President Zelensky described the latest Ukrainian strikes as "our long-range sanctions" against Russian facilities that he says finance Moscow's war. He said the Engels airfield and Saratov oil refinery were "strategic facilities". The Ukrainian military said in a separate statement that its attack triggered a blaze at the airfield - one of the main bases of Russia's strategic aviation. It said Tu-95MC and Tu-160 bombers were regularly using Engels to launch missile strikes against Ukraine. Saratov regional Governor Roman Busargin admitted that "a drone attack caused damage to civilian infrastructure in Saratov and Engels". He later said that two people were killed. Separately, three people were reported killed in a Ukrainian drone attack on a civilian vehicle in Russia's Udmurtia region, and another three in the Belgorod region bordering Ukraine. Image source, Rozetka Image caption, Ukraine's major online retailer Rozetka said its largest warehouse was hit by Russian drones overnight In the Samara region, Governor Vyacheslav Fedorishchev described a strike on a Wildberries warehouse that caused a fire as "yet another terrorist act" by Ukraine. The governor reported no casualties in the overnight attack. In recent weeks, Ukraine has hit a number of Wildberries logistics hubs, describing them as legitimate targets providing the Russian military with drone components, navigation equipment and other gear. Wildberries - often described as Russia's Amazon - employs some 48,000 people. Ukraine's attacks are reported to have had a serious impact on the Russian economy, especially on hundreds of small and mid-sized businesses using the retailer. Meanwhile, Russia has been recently targeting warehouses of Ukraine's Nova Poshta postal company and major online retailers like Rozetka. Rozetka said its largest warehouse was hit overnight by Russian drones, but reported no injuries. https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/a.text: 1:52 Typhoon Dolphin hits east China with heavy rainfall and strong winds – video China Mass evacuations in Beijing as Typhoon Dolphin brings more torrential rain to China Forecasters warned the Chinese capital could receive more than one-third of its average annual rainfall over 24 hours Yu-chen Li in Taipei Wed 12 Aug 2026 00.43 EDT Last modified on Wed 12 Aug 2026 00.44 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Thousands of people have been evacuated from areas at risk of flooding and landslides in Beijing, as the remnants of Typhoon Dolphin continue to bring torrential rain to northern and central China . Forecasters warned on Tuesday that the Chinese capital could receive more than 150mm of rain over the following 24 hours, with some districts forecast to exceed 200mm – more than one-third of Beijing’s average annual rainfall of 528mm. Beijing remained under an orange rainstorm warning, the second-highest level, on Wednesday, with the heaviest rainfall expected across the morning. Floods, storms and landslides: Typhoon Dolphin ravages China – in pictures Read more Authorities closed hundreds of tourist attractions and campsites on Wednesday, with more than 1,300 tourists evacuated or turned away. Meanwhile, over 5,000 elderly people were moved from care facilities and about 1,800 people living around construction projects in mountainous or riverside areas were relocated. View image in fullscreen A person rides an electric scooter on a flooded street while avoiding fallen bicycles in Xiangyang, Hubei province. Photograph: Go Nakamura/Reuters The rain also disrupted Wednesday morning’s commute. Official local media reported that 250 bus routes had been suspended and trains were running at reduced speeds on 10 metro lines. Dolphin, the strongest typhoon to hit China so far this year , has weakened after making landfall in the eastern province of Zhejiang on Sunday, but its remnants have continued to draw large amounts of tropical moisture deep inland and drench central and northern parts of the country. The neighbouring Hebei province was also on alert for mountain floods, landslides and other geological hazards. Authorities said they had dispatched 623 teams to mountainous areas and equipped more than 2,100 at-risk villages with satellite phones or satellite messaging terminals to maintain communications during emergencies, according to state media. View image in fullscreen Cars drive on a flooded street following heavy rain brought by Typhoon Dolphin in Taizhou, Zhejiang province. Photograph: VCG/Getty Images In the central province of Henan, authorities raised the warning for torrential rain to the highest-level red alert on Wednesday morning, as downpours continue to batter large swathes of the province. More heavy rain was forecast through Thursday morning, with 24-hour rainfall totals of up to 350mm expected in some areas. Classes, business operations and non-essential outdoor activities have been suspended in the affected areas of Henan. Residents were told to avoid deep flood waters and evacuate immediately if vehicles stall in water, state media reports. China, the world’s second-largest economy, is increasingly exposed to destructive ‌weather events that scientists link to climate change. This year is proving particularly tough due to the ​emergence of the El Niño weather pattern that is driving up temperatures and fuelling more frequent and intense typhoons. Rainfall records have also been broken elsewhere in central China . Wugang in Henan received 209.5mm in a day and Xiangyang in neighbouring Hubei recorded 169.1mm, both the highest single-day rainfall totals for August, according to state media. First Lady of Ukraine Olena Zelenska said she was pleased to share the country’s Independence Day with international guests attending the sixth Summit of First Ladies and Gentlemen in Kyiv. Among those present alongside Zelenska were Estonia’s First Lady Sirje Karis , Lithuania’s First Lady Diana Nausėdienė, Serbia’s First Lady Tamara Vučić , Finland’s Suzanne Elisabeth Innes-Stubb , Romania’s Mirabela Grădinaru, and Slovenia’s First Gentleman Aleš Musar . Olena Zelenska Their presence in Kyiv carries particular significance as Ukraine continues to face Russian attacks. Zelenska expressed gratitude for their decision to attend the summit in person, saying their presence would contribute to more substantive discussions on resilience, shared experiences and possible solutions to common challenges. The sixth Summit of First Ladies and Gentlemen provides a platform for representatives of participating countries to exchange experiences and discuss issues that extend beyond traditional political cooperation. In the Ukrainian context, resilience and international solidarity remain central themes as the country continues to defend itself against Russia’s full-scale invasion. Zelenska also thanked the leaders of the countries represented at the summit, including Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, Finnish President Alexander Stubb , Estonian President Alar Karis and Lithuanian President Gitanas Nausėda. Her message placed particular emphasis on the shared values that, she said, should underpin the future: freedom, dignity and peace. For Ukraine, the participation of European partners in the Independence Day events represents both a diplomatic gesture and a visible expression of solidarity at a time when the country remains under military pressure. Full statement by Olena Zelenska, published on X: “I am glad to share our Independence Day with Ukraine’s great friends who are present at the sixth Summit of First Ladies and Gentlemen in Kyiv. Today, beside me are my colleagues: Estonia’s First Lady Sirje Karis, Lithuania’s – Diana Nausėdienė, Serbia’s – Tamara Vučić, Finland’s – Suzanne Elisabeth Innes-Stubb, Romania’s – Mirabela Grădinaru, as well as Slovenia’s First Gentleman Aleš Musar. I am grateful for their determination to be here during this difficult period of Russian attacks. This inspires more substantive discussions about our shared resilience, experience, and solutions. Thank you for your engagement and to the leaders of the countries: Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, Finland’s – Alexander Stubb, Estonia’s – Alar Karis, Lithuania’s – Gitanas Nausėda. https://collider.com/horror-books-master.text: By Dyah Ayu Larasati Published Sep 30, 2026, 12:27 AM EDT Dyah (pronounced Dee-yah) is a Senior Author at Collider , responsible for both writing and transcription duties. She joined the website in 2022 as a Resource Writer before stepping into her current role in April 2023. As a Senior Author, she writes Features and Lists covering TV, music, and movies, making her a true Jill of all trades. In addition to her writing, Dyah also serves as an interview transcriber, primarily for events such as San Diego Comic-Con, the Toronto International Film Festival , and the Sundance Film Festival . Dyah graduated from Satya Wacana Christian University in October 2019 with a Bachelor's degree in English Literature , concentrating on Creative Writing. On March 2026, Dyah graduated with Master's degree in English Literature Studies , with a thesis on intersectionality in postcolonial-feminist studies in Asian literary works. Born and raised between Indonesia and Singapore , Dyah is no stranger to different cultures. She now resides in the small town of Kendal with her husband and four cats, where she spends her free time cooking or cycling. Sign in to your Collider account Add Us Add on Google Preferred Source Google Discover Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap It takes more than cheap scares to turn a horror book into a masterpiece. No matter the century, horror remains timeless . Whether these stories are real or not is ultimately a matter of belief, but their core is simple: They warn us about what happens when we attempt to mess with things beyond our understanding. The best horror stories don't just give personality to the paranormal; they show that humans can be just as horrifying, with their darkest instincts manifesting in the ugliness that defines the genre. From a classic haunted house to a bloodthirsty count with fangs, here are five horror books I knew would be masterpieces from the first chapter . 1 'Dracula' (1897) The original cover of the 'Dracula' novel by Bram Stoker Image via Archibald Constable and Company Bram Stoker 's Dracula set the standard for future vampire literature, influencing works like Interview with the Vampire and Salem's Lot while also paving the way for lighter takes on the genre, such as Twilight . Told through journal entries and other documents, the novel immediately feels like an intimate, firsthand account . Chapter 1, written from Jonathan Harker's perspective, follows his journey toward Count Dracula's estate, beginning with his arrival in Bistritz, in present-day Romania, where he makes several stops before reaching his destination. In today's terms, the chapter almost feels like "a day in my life" scenario, with Harker documenting his journey as it unfolds. Part of the novel's appeal is the diary-like format, which gives Harker's narration a distinct personality while making readers feel as though they are experiencing his journey alongside him. More importantly, Chapter 1 cleverly avoids explicitly describing Dracula himself. Instead, Harker learns about him through the reactions of the villagers he encounters along the way . When Harker tells them where he is headed, they cross themselves, warn him against continuing, and even urge him to cancel the trip. When he refuses, one villager gives him a crucifix for protection , despite Harker's skepticism. The horror is already brewing, not because Dracula has appeared, but because everyone around Harker seems terrified of him. 2 'The Haunting of Hill House' (1959) Image via Viking Press Apparently, there's a lot of logistics involved before anyone can conduct research on a haunted house, and Shirley Jackson captures that experience perfectly in Chapter 1 of The Haunting of Hill House . As an anthropologist with a passion for the supernatural, Dr. John Montague is determined to prove the existence of the paranormal by going straight to the source: a supposedly haunted house. The problem is that his research has neither the credibility nor the proper resources to support his claims, leaving him ridiculed by other scholars. Still, that doesn't stop him from pursuing his work, and Jackson wastes no time establishing just how seriously Montague takes his research , even when everyone else seems to think it's ridiculous. Chapter 1 is less about the actual haunting and more about everything that has to happen before Montague can even begin his investigation. From finding the right property to securing permission to stay there and selecting the people who will accompany him, there is an almost absurd amount of preparation involved. Montague even carefully considers the personalities and backgrounds of his potential assistants, because apparently studying ghosts requires good team chemistry, too. It's an amusingly mundane setup for what is supposed to be a supernatural investigation , but that's exactly why it's interesting. C OLLIDER Collider · Quiz Collider Exclusive · 8 Questions · 2 Minutes What Is Your Biggest Horror Nightmare ? Elm Street · Chucky · Scream · The Conjuring Four horror franchises. Four completely different ways of scaring you. One waits until you fall asleep. One makes sure nobody believes you. One is already in your group of friends. And one is in the house with your family. Answer eight quick questions about how you actually watch horror, and find out which nightmare was built for you. 😴 Elm Street (Freddy Krueger) 🧸 Chucky (Child's Play) 📞 Scream (Ghostface) 🕯️ The Conjuring (The Warren Files) FIND YOUR NIGHTMARE → QUESTION 1 / 8 THE SCENE 01 Which horror scene makes you cover your eyes? Four classic images. One of them is worse than the others for you. A Somebody falling asleep when they really should not. B A toy that has moved, and nobody touched it. C A phone ringing in an empty house. D A child talking to somebody who is not there. NEXT QUESTION → QUESTION 2 / 8 THE NOISE 02 You are home alone and you hear a noise. First thought? Everybody has one. It arrives before you have decided anything. A I am exhausted and my mind is playing tricks on me. B Something in this room is not where I left it. C Somebody is in here with me. D This house has never felt entirely right. NEXT QUESTION → QUESTION 3 / 8 THE RULE 03 Which horror movie rule would you break first? Everybody thinks they would survive. Almost nobody actually does. A Never fall asleep. B Never leave it out of your sight. C Never answer the phone. D Never go down to the basement. NEXT QUESTION → QUESTION 4 / 8 THE REACTION 04 Something genuinely frightening happens. What do you do? Not in a film. In your actual living room, tonight. A Convince myself I imagined the whole thing. B Tell someone, and brace for them not believing me. C Work out which person I know could be behind it. D Get everybody in the house into one room. NEXT QUESTION → QUESTION 5 / 8 MOVIE NIGHT 05 How do you actually watch a horror film? Be honest about this one. Nobody is checking. A Fine during. Wide awake at two in the morning. B Shouting at the screen that nobody is listening. C Calling the twist out loud before it lands. D Through my fingers, holding on to something. NEXT QUESTION → QUESTION 6 / 8 THE DARE 06 Somebody offers you serious money. Which do you still refuse? The amount does not matter. There is one on this list you are not doing. A Fall asleep in a room I have never been in before. B Keep an old doll on the shelf facing my bed. C Answer every unknown number that calls after midnight. D Spend one night alone in a house with a history. NEXT QUESTION → QUESTION 7 / 8 AFTER 07 Which feeling stays with you a week after the film? Good horror does not stop when the credits do. A Not wanting to turn the bedroom light off. B Not trusting one particular object in my house. C Looking twice at people I have known for years. D Feeling like something came home with me. NEXT QUESTION → QUESTION 8 / 8 THREE A.M. 08 Something wakes you at 3am. What is the worst possibility? Eight questions in, this is the one that decides your nightmare. A That I am still asleep, and it knows it. B That the thing nobody believed me about is here. C That somebody with a key is downstairs. D That something is in the doorway, watching us sleep. REVEAL MY NIGHTMARE → The Lights Just Went Out Your Nightmare Is… Four franchises, four completely different ways of getting underneath your skin. This is the one built out of your particular fear, why it works so well on you, and what it would leave behind. A Nightmare on Elm Street · Since 1984 Elm Street Your nightmare does not wait outside the door. It waits for you to close your eyes, which you are going to have to do eventually, because nobody has ever won that particular argument. Freddy is horror's cruellest idea: a threat that lives in the one place you cannot guard, cannot lock, and cannot avoid forever. You are the one who is fine during the film and wide awake at two in the morning. Your own head is where this does its damage. These films understood exhaustion as a horror engine. The kids on Elm Street do not lose because they are weak. They lose because they are tired. You can lock every door in the house. You still have to sleep. Child's Play · Chucky · Since 1988 Chucky Your nightmare is not really the doll. It is the face of the person you tell, and the way they decide, very kindly, that you have imagined all of it. Chucky works precisely because he is absurd. That is the trap: the more accurately you describe him, the less anybody is going to believe you. You are the one shouting at the screen because the characters are not listening. You know that feeling from real life too. The franchise is at its best when the adults in the room are the real obstacle, and you have met those adults. By the time somebody finally believes you, you will have handled most of it on your own. Scream · Ghostface · Since 1996 Scream Your nightmare has your number, knows your name, and has almost certainly been inside your house before. The worst part is that you already know them. Scream is the only one of these where the killer takes the mask off and turns out to be somebody who was at the party. You are the person who calls the twist out loud before it lands. You watch people the same way you watch films. The franchise made the rules of horror part of the plot, which means the survivors are the ones paying attention. You would be paying attention. Everybody is a suspect, including the person who just offered to walk you home. The Conjuring · The Warren Files · Since 2013 The Conjuring Your nightmare is not really about you. It is about the people asleep down the hall, and the feeling that whatever is here is not interested in leaving. The Conjuring films are domestic horror. The house, the family, the perfectly ordinary room that quietly stops feeling ordinary. Your instinct is to get everybody into one room. Your fear is protective rather than personal, which is rarer than it sounds. This is the one franchise where belief is the weapon. The people who come through it are the ones who are not alone and refuse to be. Whatever is here did not come for you. It came for the household, and you are the one standing in the hallway. ↻ RETAKE THE QUIZ 3 'Pet Sematary' (1983) Image via Hodder Paperbacks Pet Sematary begins in very Stephen King fashion: by picking apart the everyday flaws of ordinary people. Chapter 1 is only two pages long, but that's all King needs to establish just how chaotic the Creed family already is. Louis Creed has essentially gambled 12 years of his life by moving to Maine to work as a physician at the University of Maine. His career is respectable, but his family life is another story. His wife is anxious, his daughter is sulking, his infant son is fussy, and, to top it all off, their cat is yowling nonstop in the back of the car. Before anything supernatural happens, King makes it clear that Louis is already dealing with a family dynamic that is anything but peaceful . Told through Louis' inner thoughts, Chapter 1 also has a darkly comedic tone, particularly when he considers abandoning his family in some random town and heading to Florida instead to become a medic at Disney World. It's obviously an absurd thought, but the joke reveals something important about Louis as a father. He loves his family, yet his first instinct when things become overwhelming is to fantasize about escaping them. Even in just two pages, King establishes the flawed, relatable man whose choices will ultimately drive the story's supernatural horror. 4 'Frankenstein' (1818) The cover of 'Frankenstein' by Mary Shelley Image via Castlesync It is truly remarkable that Mary Shelley was only 18 years old when she first conceived Frankenstein . Despite her relatively young age, the novel feels as though it was written by someone far beyond her years, with beautiful prose that almost masks the horror surrounding the arrival of the titular monster. Before readers even reach Chapter 1, Frankenstein begins in an epistolary fashion , with four letters written by Robert Walton to his sister, Margaret Saville. The first recounts Walton's journey toward the North Pole in pursuit of scientific discovery, immediately establishing his pompous nature. Walton explains that he wants to make sense of the North Pole, determine whether there is a passage connecting it to other countries, and uncover the origins of its magnetism. On the surface, it sounds like a noble scientific endeavor, but Walton quickly comes across as aggressively entitled and self-centered, convinced that he is destined to make one great contribution to humanity. His ambition is admirable in theory, yet something is unsettling about how desperately he wants to prove himself . That hubris becomes crucial to Frankenstein , as Walton's pursuit of knowledge mirrors the grit that ultimately drives Victor Frankenstein to create his monster . In fact, it takes only one letter for Shelley to establish that Walton is dangerously convinced his pursuit of greatness justifies everything. 5 'The Exorcist' (1971) Despite William Peter Blatty's book being published in the '70s, The Exorcist remains the stuff of urban legends. Although it is fiction, its realistic quality has kept horror enthusiasts debating whether the story is entirely fictional or contains a shred of truth. The novel is allegedly inspired by an actual case of demonic possession from the 1940s , adding to its disturbing reputation. Before Chapter 1 begins, the prologue introduces Father Lankester Merrin, a priest and archaeologist who encounters a strange amulet associated with the demon Pazuzu . Although this happens hundreds of miles away from the United States, Pazuzu is about to become the source of someone else's nightmares in Georgetown. Chapter 1 then shifts to actress Chris MacNeil and her 11-year-old daughter, Regan, who are staying in a large rented house with their Swiss housekeepers. The chapter wastes no time establishing that something is off, with strange tapping and scratching sounds and furniture mysteriously being moved. What really stands out, though, is how the chapter establishes Chris herself before the horror fully takes over . She is an actress working in an industry that can be demanding, competitive, and filled with difficult people, yet she remains grounded in her role as a mother. That makes the strange occurrences around the house feel even more intrusive because Chris initially has no reason to suspect anything supernatural.
